thread:
rachel: paging the SRE oncall — we're seeing a sudden flood of gateway timeouts and 5xx on hosted inference in us-west-2. p95 and p99 both spiked after the recent deploy (~10:12 UTC). alert rules firing: api.error_rate > 5% and latency.p99 > 5s. @oncall-bot triggered.
oncall-bot: @channel SRE Page — Priority: P1. Incident ID: INC-20260314-177900. Pager: rachel -> sam. Runbook: https://runbook.example/timeout-regression
sam: looking now — getting dashboards. can someone post the deploy id? deploy-bot: Deploy completed: rollout/serve-evov-20260314 (sha: abcdef123) at 10:11:48 UTC. Canary passed.
lee: i'm seeing 504 gateway errors coming from gateway-nginx in front of runtime pool. error budget for host gw-xx near exhausted. logs show `upstream timed out (110: Connection timed out) while reading response header from upstream` for requests proxied to runtime-1.*
rachel: same — p95 jumped from ~120ms to 3.2s and p99 to 9s. error rate for generate endpoint ~18% over last 5m. customers: multiple small PLG apps report elevated retries.
maria: quick customer impact check — top-10 customers: 4 show increased 5xx; two have alerts open with CS. I'm messaging support to coordinate comms. @support-bot please open a customer-impact thread and tag account reps.
support-bot: Created ticket TI-9876 for impacted customers, pushed to Statuspage draft.
sam: can we isolate whether this is model runtime saturation or a networking flap? checking pod metrics: runtime-pool cpu and gpu utilization normal, but connection queue and accept backlog is spiking on the runtime proxies.
sre-bot: Observed increased syscall latencies on proxy hosts and many sockets in CLOSE_WAIT. Possible leak or slow backend responses.
lee: rolling logs from runtime show a large number of requests with KV cache warmup taking long, and some requests stuck on large context loads. suspect that a change in model loader/quantization in the deploy caused slower init path under some sequences.
rachel: mitigation options: 1) revert deploy (fastest), 2) scale proxy/replica counts + increase timeouts (mitigates while we diagnose), 3) route traffic to previous stable model variant. what's our rollback time? sam?
sam: we can rollback to previous revision (serve-evov-20260307 sha: 89beef00) via the deploy service. estimated 3-5 minutes to roll back and make steady. initiating rollback now: `kubectl -n inference rollout undo deployment/serve-evov` — kicking it off.
deploy-bot: Rollback started for rollout/serve-evov (target revision: 89beef00). Rolling back canaries, draining new pods.
lee: while rollback is in progress, i'll temporarily increase proxy upstream_read_timeout from 60s to 90s and bump worker_connections to handle backlog. pushing quick change to nginx conf on gateway pool.
rachel: also apply traffic routing: moving 30% of traffic to dedicated fallback cluster in us-east-1 to reduce load on us-west-2. sam — can you validate route table policy?
sam: yes applying policy now: `redwood route set --cluster us-east-1 --weight 30 --selector hosted-api` — done. watching metrics.
maria: support: posting initial status update: short degradation affecting latency and timeouts for some hosted API customers in us-west-2. ETA: investigating. internal CS note sent.
lee: nginx tweak applied to gateway nodes. backlog decreased slightly. some 504s still present but rate dropping from 18% -> 7% over last 3 minutes.
sam: rollback completed — new pods replaced with stable revision. health checks green. monitoring shows p95 trending down: 3.2s -> 700ms; p99 down to 1.2s. error rate now 2.1%.
avi: taking over oncall for rotation in 20m. quick handoff: root cause likely a regression in model load path that increases per-request latency under certain long-context workloads. mitigation: rollback complete, nginx timeouts increased, 30% traffic rerouted. follow-ups: detailed postmortem, add e2e canary with long context tests, add socket leak detection.
rachel: agreed. @maria please coordinate any customer follow-ups for the accounts that had retries. include note that a rollback was performed and we're doing a postmortem.
maria: will do. Statuspage: incident posted, we set severity Major and noted rollback; updating customers who opened tickets.
sam: leaving monitoring at elevated alert sensitivity for next 2 hours. setting a muted pager for non-urgent alerts. if p99 stays below 2s and error rate <1% for 30m, we'll close.
lee: capturing log snippets for debug:
```
[2026-03-14T10:12:05Z] runtime-1 generate request id=xyz connection=0x7f3a2 timed out after 5000ms waiting for kv-cache
[2026-03-14T10:12:06Z] gateway-nginx upstream timed out while reading response header from upstream, backend=runtime-1:8080
```
rachel: thanks team. final actions before handoff: open postmortem ticket PM-452, assign to eng-ml and eng-runtime; attach logs and metrics. Ravi picking oncall handoff at 10:40 UTC.
ravi: acknowledged. summary for next shift: rollback done, temporary nginx timeouts applied, 30% reroute to us-east-1, customer tickets opened, postmortem assigned. will monitor for recurrence and coordinate rollback test in staging. :thumbsup:
oncall-bot: Incident INC-20260314-177900 status -> Mitigated. Next: postmortem required. Pages reopened if error rate > 5% or p99 > 5s.
support-bot: Customer outreach queued for impacted accounts. Template used: "We experienced elevated timeouts and 5xx in us-west-2 after a deploy; traffic was rerouted and the deploy was rolled back. We're investigating and will follow up."
